Name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Creating Debug Binary
Description: The product has an ASP .NET component that contains a debug binary.
BackgroundDetails: ASP .NET applications can be configured to produce debug binaries. The debug attribute of the <compilation> tag defines whether compiled binaries should include debugging information. The use of debug binaries causes an application to provide as much information about itself as possible to the user. Such binaries are only meant to be used in a development or testing environment.

CommonConsequences.Note: Debug binaries give detailed debugging messages, which is useful in a development or testing environment, but can pose a security risk if the debug binary is deployed to production. Attackers can leverage the additional information they gain from debugging output to mount attacks targeted on the framework, database, or other resources used by the application.

DetectionMethods.Description: Automated static analysis, commonly referred to as Static Application Security Testing (SAST), can find some instances of this weakness by analyzing source code (or binary/compiled code) without having to execute it. Typically, this is done by building a model of data flow and control flow, then searching for potentially-vulnerable patterns that connect "sources" (origins of input) with "sinks" (destinations where the data interacts with external components, a lower layer such as the OS, etc.)

PotentialMitigations.Description: Avoid releasing debug binaries into the production environment. Change the debug mode to false when the application is deployed into production.

Entries.IntroText: The file web.config contains the debug mode setting. Setting debug to "true" will let the browser display debugging information.

Entries.BodyText: Change the debug mode to false when the application is deployed into production.
